instruction: Shmuel, verbatim, 2026-09-09: "I don't wanna see, like, repeating patterns all over." The Herodian ashlar is a 300 cm tile, so on a 60 m wall the same five stones appear 20 times in a grid; the Jerusalem paving is a 500 cm tile over the courts and the mount platform. The textures are accepted and are NOT re-authored: the repetition is broken in the material graph.
samplingModeNote: No ddx/ddy anywhere; the sampler takes its own derivatives from a UV that is smooth within a cell and an integer away from smooth across one. Gives up the one-pixel seam guard at each bed joint and at each mirror flip; keeps hardware mip selection. Needs TA_WRAP on every variant texture.

technique.uvBandOffset: Each course band (one tile high in the plane's v axis) is slid along u by a hash of its own band index alone. Because the shift does not depend on u, it is constant along the whole wall and introduces NO vertical seam anywhere; it appears only across a bed joint, which is what running bond is. Cost: about 6 ALU. It is the single most effective free technique here: it takes the one-tile vertical autocorrelation from 1.000 to 0.211 on the Ashlar.
technique.uvCellMirror: Each tile cell is mirrored in u by a hash of its cell index. A mirrored cell still meets its neighbours edge to edge because the tile is periodic, so this is seamless too, and mirroring only in u leaves the bed joints, the per-course setback ledge (which leans out at the TOP of each stone) and the downward weather run-off exactly where they were. The sampled normal's u component is negated to match. Cost: about 5 ALU.
technique.macroVariation: Two very-low-frequency noise bands at deliberately non-harmonic periods multiply albedo brightness and shift it slightly warm or cool over tens of metres, so no two stretches of a long wall read the same even where the tile itself repeats. Cost: 2 texture fetches in the albedo node.
technique.detailBreakup: The second (mid) band also modulates roughness in the ARM node at a period non-harmonic with both the tile and the macro band, so the specular response stops repeating with the albedo. Cost: 1 texture fetch in the ARM node.
technique.perInstanceRandom: PerInstanceRandom (NOT PerInstanceCustomData) drives a per-instance value jitter. PerInstanceCustomData is the right tool when the spawner can be taught to write it - Scripts/release_crowd_tint_fix.py is this project's precedent - but the 1.44 km precinct wall's HISM instances are built in the enclosure actor's BeginPlay from its WallMaterial property, and teaching that spawner to write custom data would mean editing another pass's script or C++, which this pass may not do. PerInstanceRandom needs no spawner change at all. It returns exactly 0.0 on non-instanced components, so the HLSL treats 0.0 as 'not instanced' and applies no jitter there. Cost: about 3 ALU.
technique.rejectedStochastic: Stochastic / texture-bombing sampling (per-cell random offset, three taps blended over a triangle grid; Heitz & Neyret 2018) was implemented and MEASURED, in both the linear and the variance-preserving blend, and is NOT shipped on these materials. It removes the grid almost completely - the tile-comb energy fraction falls from 1.000 to 0.009 - but it blends three differently-offset copies of a STRUCTURED coursed-ashlar tile, and the horizontal bed joints triplicate and smear: the row-profile contrast that expresses the coursing drops to 0.12x of baseline on the Ashlar and 0.10x on the paving. That is not less repetitive masonry, it is destroyed masonry. Texture bombing is for stochastic source images. The numbers are in the manifest under measurement.<variant>.schemes.stochastic and .stochasticVP so the judgement can be re-argued from data.
technique.triplanarAxisCheck: The master keeps M_PBR_Tiled's explicit triplanar projection and its blendExponent of 4.0 unchanged, so no surface changes which plane it samples. The world-space projection does put every wall on the same global 300 cm grid - that is what makes coursing continue around a corner and it is deliberate - and the band offset and mirror hashes are computed from GLOBAL cell indices, so two faces meeting at a corner still agree.
technique.samplingMode: Texture2DSampleGrad with derivatives taken from the CONTINUOUS pre-warp UV (with the mirror sign applied to the u component). Without this, the one-pixel row where the band offset jumps would select the coarsest mip and draw a blurred line at every bed joint. The UV handed to the sampler is wrapped into [0,1), so the result does not depend on the texture's address mode - which matters because T_JerusalemPaving_BaseColor is imported TA_MIRROR while the architecture textures are TA_WRAP.
technique.samplingModeSwitch: 2026-09-10. The samplingMode note above reasoned about the one-pixel band-offset row and then assumed derivative VALIDITY was settled - that is the assumption that failed. Sampling is now a switch, -AntiRepeatSampling=grad|implicit|analytic, and the mode is stamped into every receipt as samplingMode with a one-line note. 'grad' is byte-identical to the 2026-09-09 HLSL and is proved so offline by regenerating both from the same module; it stays the default so the A side of the A/B cannot drift. 'implicit' is the fix: no ddx/ddy at all, and the warp re-expressed so the UV handed to the sampler is smooth within a cell and an integer away from smooth across one - an unmirrored cell samples uu, a mirrored cell samples (2*ci + 1) - uu, which is the same reflection the wrapped form performed. It gives up exactly the one-pixel seam guard this note was written about, at each bed joint and at each mirror flip, and it needs TA_WRAP on every variant texture because the hand wrap into [0,1) is what made the address mode irrelevant; do_build reads the address modes off the assets and refuses unless -AntiRepeatAllowMirrorAddress says otherwise. 'analytic' keeps the wrapped UV and the seam guard and takes the gradients from Nanite's analytic Parameters.WorldPosition_DDX/DDY with a hardware fallback; it is an experiment arm, not the shipping candidate, because it still reads pixel-parameter fields from author-written HLSL.

statistics.why: every counter read back 0: -nullrhi builds no shader map, so instruction and sampler counts are not measurable in this process. The exact per-pixel texture fetch count in shaderCost.textureFetchesPerPixel is counted from the graph and is the honest cost figure here.

diskResolvedSummary.why: Every pointer was resolved through the asset registry AND against the .uasset on disk after save and reopen, and its sha256 recorded. A null or unresolved pointer raises rather than being reported as a number that happens to agree with itself.

repetitionNumbers.renderedFrameMeasurement: NOT ATTEMPTED. A real-RHI capture is what would measure the shipped pixels; this machine cannot run one (captures get killed). Nothing here claims a rendered result.
repetitionNumbers.metricNote: combEnergyFraction is the fraction of non-DC 2-D spectral power on the harmonic comb of the tile period: 1.0 is wallpaper. acPeakU/acPeakV are the normalized autocorrelation one tile across and one tile up. courseProfileVsBaseline and edgeEnergyVsBaseline are QUALITY guards - a scheme that lowers the comb by flattening those has destroyed the masonry, which is exactly why stochastic bombing is not shipped.

measuredFrameContext.note: Base-pass shading is 0.84 ms of a 17.0 ms GPU frame and the frame is game-thread bound at 28.7 ms. Shadow depth passes do not evaluate base colour, so this pass adds nothing to the 1.15 ms ShadowDepths. No frame time is claimed here: this machine cannot run a real-RHI capture.
